read.thesis: Potash is the supply-side story: 2026 volume guidance raised to 14.2–14.8Mt and capex cut $50M, while phosphate EBITDA fell 75% to $23M on sulfur costs.

capex.quote: we have reduced our capital expenditures guidance by $50 million to a range of $1.95 billion to $2.05 billion

triggers.label: Potash volume guidance raised to 14.2–14.8Mt
triggers.quote: We raised the bottom end of our 2026 potash sales volumes guidance to 14.2 million to 14.8 million tonnes
triggers.highlight: We raised the bottom end of our 2026 potash sales volumes guidance

triggers.label: Capex guidance cut $50M
triggers.quote: we have reduced our capital expenditures guidance by $50 million to a range of $1.95 billion to $2.05 billion
triggers.highlight: reduced our capital expenditures guidance by $50 million

triggers.label: Potash net selling price $248 → $267/t
triggers.quote: Potash net selling price $267 per tonne in the second quarter, representing an increase from $248 per tonne

triggers.label: Phosphate EBITDA down 75% to $23M
triggers.quote: elevated sulfur costs, which have placed unsustainable pressure on global phosphate producer margins
triggers.highlight: unsustainable pressure on global phosphate producer margins

triggers.label: Retail phosphate volumes down 10%, nitrogen 7%
triggers.quote: North American retail volumes declined 10% for phosphate and 7% for nitrogen in the second quarter

guidance.quote: We raised the bottom end of our 2026 potash sales volumes guidance to 14.2 million to 14.8 million tonnes
We've maintained our forecast for global potash shipments of 74 million to 77 million tonnes in 2026
We maintained our full year retail adjusted EBITDA guidance of $1.75 billion to $1.95 billion
we have reduced our capital expenditures guidance by $50 million to a range of $1.95 billion to $2.05 billion
We continue to target our controllable cash cost below $60 per tonne on a full year basis for 2026
We maintained our 2026 nitrogen sales volume guidance of 9.2 million to 9.7 million tonnes
We maintained our 2026 phosphate sales volume guidance
have stepped up our repurchase pace in the third quarter to approximately $75 million per month

red_flags.label: Phosphate margins unsustainable on sulfur costs
red_flags.quote: elevated sulfur costs, which have placed unsustainable pressure on global phosphate producer margins

it's a difficult one to answer
